<meta>continues from the previous page where Karna vows to defeat the Pandavas</meta>

I will certainly defeat all the assembled Pandavas today. 58

Duryodhana said:
I will do all of this just as you think best, Karna. O son of a charioteer <note>original: "sūtaja", referring to Karna's foster-caste</note>, the chariots with their quivers attached will follow you closely. 59
Let carts carry for you the <term>nārācas</term> <gloss>iron-tipped arrows</gloss> and <term>ardhapaksas</term> <gloss>half-feathered arrows</gloss>.

<column-break/>

We and all the other kings will follow you, Karna. 60

Sanjaya said:
O Great King, having spoken thus, your powerful son, the King <note>Duryodhana</note>, approached the King of Madra <note>Shalya</note> and spoke these words. 61

->Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the Book of Karna of the glorious Mahabharata. 22<-

---

## 23

Sanjaya said:
O Great King, your son, having approached the King of Madra with humility, spoke these words out of affection. 1
O you who are devoted to truth, O highly fortunate one, you who increase the sorrow of your enemies.

<summary>Duryodhana agrees to provide Karna with logistical support and full military backing before approaching Shalya, the King of Madra, with a humble request.</summary>
